title.narrative: Enhancing urban coastal ecosystems for community wellbeing, climate action and biodiversity in the kingdom of Bahrain

description.narrative:
The Kingdom of Bahrain has witnessed major urban changes and notable socio-economic transformation by virtue of the rapid urbanization and climate change. As a Small Island Developing State, Bahrain is particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change, especially along the coast, where accelerating sea level rise will likely result in considerable economic loss, and urban and environmental degradation. In addition, the significant increase in population of the Kingdom of Bahrain, in tandem with the geographical limitations in terms of land size (765.3 km²), have put significant stress on the country’s resources and increased the need for collaborative work to meet the accelerating demands of the growing population.
Many efforts have been made by the Government in view of the urban and environment transformations of the last twenty years, reflecting the priorities set in the Sustainable Development Goals. The Bahrain 2030 National Planning Development Strategy, developed in 2007, guides the development new national infrastructure and is designed to address the role of sustainable land use development in generating a stable, predictable, and long-term economic growth. The Strategy addresses several issues including natural resource preservation, infrastructure development and housing reformation. It also highlights the lack of a strategic vision for green public spaces in Bahrain and deplores the limited access to public open spaces in relation to the size of the population, emphasizing the need for enhanced natural parks and urban public spaces.
The proposed 3-year project aims to rehabilitate and restore mangrove habitats situated along the urban fringes of the Bahrain capital city of Manama creating greater opportunities for recreation, awareness and ecotourism, while contributing to the broader national efforts on climate mitigation and adaptation.
By restoring urban coastal habitat, and particularly mangroves, the project aims to contribute to enhancing ‘blue natural carbon sinks’ in Bahrain together with co-benefits from protection of biodiversity, while creating opportunities for urban communities to enjoy nature-based activities that can enhance overall human well-being among the urban populations in Manama. At the same time, the project will explore and document broader socio-economic benefits of coastal ecosystems, as well as barriers and opportunities to scaling up such actions at the national level. The project will support and extend the benefits from existing work of the Bahrain Supreme Council for the Environment to restore mangrove ecosystems and to build a visitor center at Ras Sanad in Tubli Bay, and explore with stakeholders the capacity gaps for planning and sustainable management of the coastal zone as well as the possibilities for creating a ‘City Marine Park’ for Tubli Bay and showcasing Ras Sanad. The project will address some of the major barriers to progress in accelerating active restoration in complex urban settings including technical knowledge, integrated planning, inadequate resources and lack of adequate opportunities.
This project is funded under the HSBC Climate Programme 4-year global philanthropic initiative, focusing on identifying and scaling innovative and impactful solutions to climate change which are currently not commercially viable. The programme comprises funded charitable projects in every HSBC region with the goal to enable systemic change by supporting an enabling regulatory & policy environment, demonstrate the commercial viability of sustainable business models, and promote the possibility of market development & financing. The scope for HSBC MENAT is nature-based solutions to Climate Change. HSBC Sustainability Programme has two Global Partners: WWF and WRI. WWF is leading several ecosystem restoration projects in the context of this programme is potentially considered as an Implemeting Partner to lead restoration and carbon sink activities in this project.
